newsitem.title: UK: No booze please, says losing English darts team.
newsitem.headline: No booze please, says losing English darts team.

text.p: The captain of a pub darts team whose members each down 10 pints of beer during a game has banned drinking in a bid to halt their losing streak.
The Mug House players have suffered more than 50 straight defeats and have finished bottom of the local league in Upton Snodsbury, central England for the past four years.
"We get over-excited if anyone scores over 30. One regular feature is for members of our team to miss the board completely," admitted pub landlord and darts player John Adkins.

"Our captain Chris Gillard once scored nil after three darts," he said. "Another of our players threw a dart which missed the board and went into the scorer's arm. It certainly made him stand further back."
"I think we all drink too much. That's the big problem," Adkins told reporters.
Gillard said he had asked the team to stop drinking for a month to see if things improved but was not overly optimistic.

"The trouble is that some of our players need four or five pints to boost their confidence," he said. "If they don't have a drink they are uptight, and if they do they fall over and face the wrong way."
